name: RetroArch

launch.notes: ES-DE: %EMULATOR_RETROARCH% %EXTRA_CONFIGFILE%=%EXTERNALDATA%/Android/data/%ANDROIDPACKAGE%/files/retroarch.cfg %EXTRA_LIBRETRO%=%INTERNALDATA%/%ANDROIDPACKAGE%/cores/<core>_libretro_android.so %EXTRA_ROM%=%ROM%. ES-DE expands %INTERNALDATA% to /data/user/<userid> and %EXTERNALDATA% to /storage/emulated/<userid> (https://gitlab.com/es-de/emulationstation-de/-/raw/master/es-app/src/FileData.cpp); the app uses user 0. RetroArch uses legacy file paths, not SAF URIs, so {romPath} is a real filesystem path derived from the SAF document ID ('primary:ROMs/snes/x.sfc' -> '/storage/emulated/0/ROMs/snes/x.sfc'; '<VOLUME-UUID>:path' -> '/storage/<VOLUME-UUID>/path'). The core must already be installed inside RetroArch or it shows a black screen (ANDROID-DEV.md).

configTarget.folderToGrant: The RetroArch base folder in shared storage, normally /storage/emulated/0/RetroArch (it contains the 'config' folder).
configTarget.notes: Game override = <config dir>/<core library_name>/<content file name without extension>.cfg containing only the differing keys (config_load_override in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libretro/RetroArch/master/configuration.c). On Android the config dir is <parent>/config where <parent> = /storage/emulated/0/RetroArch when shared storage is writable, else Android/data/<pkg>/files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libretro/RetroArch/master/frontend/drivers/platform_unix.c). If the granted folder has no 'config' subfolder the app must fall back to export + manual copy. Format: one 'key = "value"' per line (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libretro/RetroArch/master/retroarch.cfg).

settings.label: Run-ahead
settings.description: Runs frames ahead in the background and rolls back to cut input lag. Costs CPU roughly per extra frame.

settings.label: Run-ahead frames
settings.description: How many frames to run ahead. Match the game's internal lag (usually 1-2); too many causes visible jitter.

settings.label: Run-ahead second instance
settings.description: Uses a second core instance for run-ahead, which avoids audio glitches with many cores. On by default in RetroArch.

settings.label: Preemptive frames
settings.description: Alternative latency reduction that only re-runs frames when input changes. Do not combine with run-ahead.

settings.label: Integer scaling
settings.description: Scale only by whole numbers for perfectly even pixels (adds borders).

settings.label: Bilinear filtering
settings.description: Smooths pixels when scaling. Off (RetroArch's Android default) gives sharp pixels.

settings.label: Shaders enabled
settings.description: Master switch for shader presets (the preset itself is chosen inside RetroArch). On by default; it only matters once a preset is loaded.

settings.label: Frame delay (ms)
settings.description: Waits before running the core each frame to reduce latency; too high causes stutter.

settings.label: Audio latency (ms)
settings.description: Audio buffer size. RetroArch uses 128 ms on Android because 64 ms is too low for most devices. Lower it only if you hear no crackling.

settings.label: Show FPS
settings.description: On-screen FPS counter for test sessions.

presets.name: Thor Low Latency (8/16-bit)
presets.description: Run-ahead 1 frame with a second instance, sharp pixels. For NES/SNES/Genesis/GBA cores.

values.reason: Run-ahead is the documented way to remove built-in game lag; light 8/16-bit cores have ample CPU headroom on Snapdragon 8 Gen 2.
Docs: lag frames = frames until the action shows minus 1; 1 is the safe default for most games.
Secondary-core mode described in the run-ahead guide.
Preference for crisp pixel art on a 1080p OLED.
Required by this app's test procedure.

presets.name: Thor Balanced
presets.description: No run-ahead (lowest power), smooth scaling. Good for N64/PS1 cores.

values.reason: Run-ahead multiplies core CPU cost; the guide warns the machine must run the core that many times faster.

values.description: Bilinear filtering: a softer image instead of sharp pixels.
values.reason: N64 and PS1 output (240p-480i with 3D geometry) is scaled by a non-integer factor to the 1080p panel; bilinear filtering hides the uneven pixel sizes. This is a taste choice, not RetroArch's default (config.def.h sets video_smooth off on Android).
Required by this app's test procedure.

presets.name: Thor Pixel Perfect
presets.description: Integer scaling with sharp pixels; run-ahead 1 frame.

values.reason: Even pixel sizes; 1080p divides cleanly by 224-line (4x = 896) and 240-line (4x = 960) content.
Required by this app's test procedure.

manualNotes: Use the 64-bit RetroArch from retroarch.com; ES-DE reports the Play Store build lacks cores and can fail to launch from frontends (https://gitlab.com/es-de/emulationstation-de/-/raw/master/ANDROID-DEV.md).
Shader presets (.slangp) are chosen inside RetroArch; this app only toggles video_shader_enable in v1.
Core options (.opt files) are out of scope for v1.
